Subject: Backup retention exceptions and deletion SLA for audit logs

Hi Samira — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap and next steps from our side so procurement/security have a single thread to reference.

Call recap (high level):
- Healthly is evaluating Redwood for inference hosting for PII-linked processing. Core asks were SOC 2 status, GDPR/HIPAA alignment, and specifics on log/backups deletion SLAs for audit evidence.
- You requested an example of our retention playbook, timelines for deletion from primary + backup stores, and a short note Procurement can attach to their risk assessment.

Commitments / immediate answers:
1) SOC 2: Redwood has an ongoing SOC 2 Type II program; Type II report expected to be completed by Q3 2028. We will provide the report as soon as it’s issued and can provide interim artifacts (control matrices and SOC scope) this week.
2) Retention windows (default hosted offering):
   - Operational request traces (per-request metadata, latency traces): 90 days in hot store.
   - Audit/auth events (API key use, user management events): 400 days for customers on enterprise plans; 90 days for standard plan.
   - Backups/snapshots (encrypted, immutable snapshots): retained 3 years by default; eligible for early deletion per request subject to snapshot-chain constraints (see below).
3) Deletion SLA and process:
   - Primary store deletion requests: Redwood will remove records from the primary datastore within 30 days of an approved erase request.
   - Backup/snapshot deletion: due to replication and immutable snapshot chaining, removal from cold storage can take up to 60 calendar days after the primary deletion is completed.
   - Legal hold & exceptions: items placed on legal hold will not be deleted until the hold is removed; this overrides deletion SLAs.
4) Encryption & keys:
   - Hosted: backups and logs are encrypted at rest with Redwood-managed CMKs; customer CMK (BYOK) is available for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Attachments: I attached the retention playbook (Retention_Playbook_v2.docx) and a blank vendor security questionnaire if you want to drop it into your tracker; Ben will follow up with a short procurement-friendly note.

Next steps:
- Ben to answer the snapshot-chain question and provide a template procurement blurb (action: Ben, by EOD Wed).
- Samira to confirm whether Healthly wants enterprise retention (400 days) or standard (90 days) and whether Legal wants a hard legal-hold clause in the MSA (action: Samira).

Happy to hop on a 15-min follow-up if it speeds things up.

Thanks,
Tessa
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Samira — thanks for the great questions. I’m Redwood’s security liaison for this engagement; below are specifics and the procurement blurb you can paste.

Mechanics of the 60-day backup deletion window:
- We create incremental snapshots nightly and perform a full snapshot weekly. Snapshots are chained to enable point-in-time restores; because of chunk-level deduplication and immutability in our deep-cold repository, expunge operations require rebuilding affected chain indexes which is why removal from cold storage can take up to 60 calendar days.
- For Dedicated/Private customers with custom retention, we can schedule targeted snapshot pruning that shortens this window (typically to 14–21 days) with an agreed operational playbook.

400-day audit/auth events retention: configurable?
- Yes. The 400-day default for enterprise customers is a configurable policy parameter. Contractual minimum we can commit to is 180 days on enterprise plans (shorter windows require C-level signoff due to audit implications).

Encryption & key mgmt:
- Hosted customers without BYOK are provisioned per-customer envelope keys; CMKs are managed by Redwood but are logically scoped per-customer. Keys are rotated annually by default; immediate rotation on-demand is possible with a signed change ticket.

Procurement blurb (copy/paste):
"Redwood Inference confirms the following deletion and retention behavior for hosted customers: primary datastore erasure will be completed within 30 calendar days of an approved deletion request. Removal of affected data from backup/snapshot cold storage may take up to 60 calendar days due to immutable snapshot chaining and deep-cold repository processing. Items subject to a legal hold will not be removed until the hold is lifted. Redwood provides enterprise customers configurable retention parameters and can accelerate snapshot pruning for Dedicated/Private deployments under a documented operational plan."

Attached evidence: I uploaded the control matrix, backup deletion SOP, and a one-page diagram of our snapshot lifecycle to the Drive link Tessa provided. I also filled sections 4–7 of your Vendor_Security_Q.pdf and re-uploaded a redlined copy to the same folder.

If helpful, I can join your procurement call Friday morning for 10–15 mins to answer any live questions.

-Ben
